interest: Shows 1931 market panic from Britain's gold exit and the Mukden Incident, and 1933 fallout from Japan's League exit.
overview: This file (decimal file 894.5171, covering October 1931 to March 1933) contains U.S. State Department records, cross-reference sheets, and an internal memorandum concerning financial conditions, securities markets, and related legal issues in Japan. The file documents two major episodes of distress on the Tokyo Stock Exchange: the trading suspension in late September 1931 triggered by Britain's departure from the gold standard and heightened tensions in Manchuria and China, which was stabilized by an emergency loan from the Nomura Bank of Osaka; and the severe market collapse in February 1933, precipitated by post-gold embargo inflation, rising industrial costs, and Japan's announced secession from the League of Nations. In addition, the file includes a Division of Far Eastern Affairs memorandum addressing a tax exemption claim on perpetual lease property in Yokohama asserted by an American citizen, Dr. Worden, which the U.S. Embassy declined to support under existing treaties.

subfiles.about: Report on the suspension of trading on the Tokyo Stock Exchange in September 1931 following Britain's suspension of gold payments and the Manchurian crisis.
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 351: the Tokyo exchange closed September 25-28, 1931 after panic selling tied to Britain's gold suspension and Manchurian anxiety; a 3,400,000-yen Nomura Bank loan to brokers resolved the crisis.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet with Attached Extract from Despatch No. 351 on Tokyo Stock Exchange Suspension

subfiles.about: Report on the collapse of the Tokyo stock market in February 1933, price indices, unfavorable trade balances, and an impending iron industry merger.
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 1939: February 1933's Tokyo stock collapse erased about half a billion yen, driven by gold-embargo inflation, Japan's League withdrawal, and rising costs; wholesale prices fell 2.9%, the trade deficit reached 126,647,000 yen, and a state iron-and-steel merger was planned.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet with Attached Extract from Despatch No. 1939 on the Tokyo Stock Market Collapse and Economic Conditions

subfiles.about: Memorandum reviewing an American citizen's claim of income tax exemption on perpetual lease rental property in Yokohama.
subfiles.summary: Memo concurs that Dr. Worden of Yokohama cannot claim treaty-based income-tax exemption on his perpetual lease property, since leases are private contracts, barring evidence of anti-American discrimination.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Dr. Worden's Income Tax Exemption Claim on Perpetual Lease Property
